title: Motion Evaluation

C.description: Temporal-enabled model (with temporal modules and fusion)

D.description: Temporal-disabled ablation (C checkpoint with temporal disabled)

key_findings.temporal_motion_impact: Experiment C shows 32% higher displacement (2.08 vs 1.57 px) compared to B and D
key_findings.direction_control: Experiment C has lower direction accuracy (47.5% vs 50.6%) despite higher motion
key_findings.ablation_validation: Experiments B and D have identical metrics, confirming temporal module behavior
key_findings.temporal_quality: All experiments have nearly identical smoothness scores (~0.0156-0.0157)

conclusions.primary: Temporal processing increases motion magnitude but does not improve directional control
secondary: Temporal modules function as designed (confirmed by ablation)
Directional control remains unresolved across all configurations
Temporal-enabled model struggles more with stationary prompts

recommendations: Investigate text conditioning integration with temporal modules
Develop enhanced motion evaluation metrics (optical flow)
Examine systematic failure in downward motion direction
